```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7,
                      fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 80)
```

cytokineR takes bead-based multiplex immunoassay data (Bio-Rad Bio-Plex,
Luminex xMAP) from the instrument export to analysis-ready values in small,
visible steps. Every step is a swappable *method* that records what it
estimated, so the whole pre-processing can be inspected, reproduced and
compared with alternatives.

```{r}
library(cytokineR)
```

## 1. Import

`read_bioplex()` reads Bio-Plex Manager exports (multi-analyte blocks or one
sheet per analyte, Excel or CSV) and `read_xponent()` reads Luminex xPONENT
CSV files. Give several files at once to read one plate per file. Anything
else can be brought in with `cyto_from_long()` or `cyto_from_wide()`.

```{r}
f <- system.file("extdata", "bioplex_multi_example.csv", package = "cytokineR")
plate1 <- read_bioplex(f, plate = "P1", batch = "1")
plate1
head(cyto_data(plate1)[, c("well", "sample_type", "sample_id", "level",
                           "analyte", "fi", "expected_conc", "vendor_conc",
                           "vendor_flag")])
```

Sample types come from the Bio-Plex type codes (`S1`..`S8`, `B`, `C1`..,
`X1`..). The description field becomes the sample id, so name your wells in
Bio-Plex Manager. If the assigned standard concentrations are not in the
export, add them with `standards_series()` and `set_standards()` (one table
per kit lot, using a `batch` column). Study metadata is joined with
`annotate_samples()`.

The rest of this vignette uses `cyto_example`, a simulated study with two
batches (kit lots) of three plates, controls on every plate and bridging
samples measured in both batches. Because it is simulated, the true
concentrations are known (column `truth`).

```{r}
x <- cyto_example
x
```

## 2. Quality control

Flags never delete data. They mark rows in the `qc` column and, by default,
stop them from being used to *estimate* corrections (`use_for_fit = FALSE`).

```{r}
x <- flag_beads(x, min_count = 35)
x <- flag_replicates(x, max_cv = 0.3, types = c("standard", "control"))
table(x$data$qc)
```

PCA of the study samples shows how much of the main variation is plate or
batch, and which plates stand out:

```{r}
p <- qc_pca(cyto_transform(x, "log2"))
p$group_r2
plot(p, color = "batch")
```

`qc_plates()` combines robust z-scores of samples, blanks, standards and
controls with the PCA distance; `qc_controls()` gives Levey-Jennings charts
with Westgard rules for the control materials:

```{r}
qc_plates(x)
plot(qc_controls(x), analytes = c("IL-6", "IL-8", "IP-10"))
```

## 3. Processing steps

There are four stages, each with several registered methods:

```{r}
cyto_methods()
```

Steps can be called directly ...

```{r}
y <- x |>
  cyto_transform("log2") |>
  cyto_normalize("anchor", anchors = "ctrl_low", by = "plate", scope = "batch") |>
  cyto_correct_batch("bridge")
y
```

... and every step keeps its estimates, e.g. the plate offsets estimated by
the anchor step:

```{r}
cyto_steps(y)[, c("step", "stage", "method", "note")]
i <- which(cyto_steps(y)$method == "anchor")
head(cyto_fit(y, step = i))
plot_corrections(y, step = i)
```

Before and after:

```{r, fig.height = 5}
plot_plates(cyto_transform(x, "log2"), analytes = c("IL-6", "IL-8", "VEGF"))
plot_plates(y, analytes = c("IL-6", "IL-8", "VEGF"))
```

## 4. Concentrations

`cyto_calibrate()` converts signal to concentration. Besides the usual
per-plate 5PL there is a model-free monotone interpolation (`spline`) and a
shared-shape 5PL that borrows strength across the plates of a kit lot
(`shared`); see `vignette("signal-scales")`.

```{r}
cx <- cyto_calibrate(x, "shared")
plot_standards(cx, analytes = c("IL-6", "IL-10", "TNF-a"))
head(cyto_fit(cx)$curves)
```

Values outside the working range are censored (`NA`, with their limits kept)
and can be imputed:

```{r}
cx <- cyto_impute(cx, "rank_tobit")
cx
```

## 5. Pipelines and output

The same processing written as a pipeline object can be stored, printed,
re-run and benchmarked:

```{r}
p <- cyto_pipeline(
  pipe_custom(function(x) flag_beads(x, 35), label = "beads"),
  pipe_calibrate("shared"),
  pipe_impute("rank_tobit"),
  pipe_correct_batch("bridge"),
  name = "shared curve"
)
p
z <- run_pipeline(cyto_example, p)
cyto_steps(z)[, c("step", "stage", "method", "scale_after", "note")]
```

`cyto_wide()` gives the usual one-row-per-sample table for statistics:

```{r}
w <- cyto_wide(z)
head(w[, c("plate", "sample_id", "subject", "time", "IL-6", "IL-8")])
```
